core_obligations: Invoke the characterization criterion for weak Serre subcategories and reduce, using the section's results on cokernels and extensions, to showing that the kernel of a map F -> G between objects of A lies in A (proof lines 5691-5700).
Choose finite presentations of F and of G by direct sums of A_U = j_{U!}O_U with U in the basis, and refine them using the covering-surjection lemma (proof lines 5701-5710 and following).
Exhibit the kernel as the kernel of a map between finite direct sums of the standard objects, so that the assumed hypothesis applies and the kernel lies in A, completing the proof up to line 5731.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the kernel of a map between objects of A via the weak Serre criterion.
Present both objects finitely and refine the presentations.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in the quasi-compact objects situation the full subcategory A of modules isomorphic to a cokernel presentation by direct images j_{U!}O_U along basis members is a weak Serre subcategory, provided the kernel of every map between finite direct sums of such objects already lies in A. The proof uses the characterization criterion for weak Serre subcategories and the section's closure results for cokernels and extensions, reducing the verification to the kernel of a map between two objects of A; it then chooses presentations of both objects and refines them, so that the kernel can be exhibited as an object of A by the assumed hypothesis (proof lines 5690-5731). H2: the reduction chain to the single kernel case and the refinement of the two presentations are the substance, and the argument is written out.
